diagrams.title: Operate a Bid Desk, Not an Influence Channel
diagrams.subtitle: Five evidence-backed handoffs from supplier intake to service billing.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The operator sells procurement support to supplier clients. Government contract face value and subcontract principal remain outside recognized operator service revenue. Federal and municipal solicitations require separate rule matrices.
diagrams.caption: Automate solicitation alerts, bid calendars, and checklist reminders; retain named human ownership of eligibility, pricing, and submission.

stages.label: Qualify the supplier
stages.detail: Record client authority, past performance, delivery resources, cash requirements, and conflicts. Check SAM.gov registration and exclusions where relevant; verify claimed set-aside status rather than treating a profile entry as sufficient evidence.

stages.label: Screen the opportunity
stages.detail: Use SAM.gov saved searches and municipal purchasing portals. Extract mandatory qualifications, place of performance, response deadlines, amendments, and evaluation factors into a solicitation matrix with a named pursuit owner.

stages.label: Design the service
stages.detail: Define fixed-scope or retainer deliverables, client responsibilities, and acceptance evidence. Review contingent-fee restrictions and proposed teaming structures before signing; a fixed fee does not cure prohibited conduct.

stages.label: Prepare and submit
stages.detail: Maintain a dated bid calendar, assign technical sections, validate required representations, and obtain client signoff. Have the authorized submitter retain the final package, amendment acknowledgments, and portal receipt.

stages.label: Deliver and collect
stages.detail: Record completed service milestones and invoice under the client agreement. Track receivables aging and supplier performance separately; recognize earned service fees without booking the client's government award as operator revenue.

diagrams.title: One Annual Client Cohort, Five Nested Stages
diagrams.subtitle: 200 screened suppliers become 20 signed and served clients.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative mature-year acquisition cohort, not measured conversion data. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage, counted by unique supplier organization. All 20 final clients receive a full year of services averaging $28,000 each; partial-year starts would require a separate revenue schedule.
diagrams.caption: 200 to 80 to 40 to 25 to 20 produces 10% end-to-end conversion and $560,000 Base-Case recognized service revenue. Signed service clients are not government contract awards.

stages.label: Screened suppliers
stages.detail: Select suppliers with a defined public-sector offering, reachable decision-makers, and a plausible delivery footprint. Count each organization once, even when it pursues multiple solicitations through different purchasing portals.

stages.label: Capability-qualified suppliers
stages.detail: Confirm relevant capability evidence, resource availability, and procurement fit. Remove organizations seeking access payments, unsupported certifications, or opportunities they cannot perform with the proposed team.

stages.label: Completed discovery engagements
stages.detail: Complete a structured discovery meeting with an authorized buyer. Establish bid volume, service boundaries, payment capacity, and which activities remain with the client's technical and pricing owners.

stages.label: Issued service proposals
stages.detail: Issue scoped service proposals only after reviewing fee structure, conflicts, and delivery effort. Include milestone acceptance, invoice timing, and workload limits rather than promising a government award.

stages.label: Signed and served clients
stages.detail: Deliver the modeled annual service mix: four clients at each of $40,000, $30,000, $28,000, $24,000, and $18,000. Total recognized fees equal $560,000 across 20 clients.

diagrams.title: Base Case: $560,000 Revenue to $126,000 Owner Net
diagrams.subtitle: Four expense deductions reconcile exactly to a 22.5% net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: USD per mature operating year. The first bar is recognized service revenue, the next four bars are signed expense movements, and the sixth bar is the closing total, not another movement. Expense allocation is illustrative; revenue, net margin, and owner net match the canonical Base Case.
diagrams.caption: $560,000 - $210,000 - $140,000 - $60,000 - $24,000 = $126,000; $126,000 / $560,000 = 22.5%. Costs total $434,000. No client award principal enters this bridge.

stages.label: Recognized service revenue
stages.detail: Recognize earned bid-desk and teaming-support fees under client service agreements. Exclude government award face value, client purchasing volume, and funds that merely pass through for another party.

stages.label: Direct contract delivery
stages.detail: Allocate aggregate project-based compensation to the three contractor seats covering capture analysis, proposal production, and delivery verification. Remaining contribution after this deduction is $350,000.

stages.label: Full-time personnel
stages.detail: Budget total loaded compensation for two full-time seats at an illustrative $70,000 each. Verify actual hiring costs before adopting this allocation. Remaining contribution after personnel expense is $210,000.

stages.label: Operating infrastructure
stages.detail: Allocate $24,000 to software and secure document operations, $18,000 to external legal and accounting services, and $18,000 to insurance, selling, and administration. These outside services do not create dedicated pod seats.

stages.label: Rework and credit losses
stages.detail: Model $16,000 of unrecovered delivery rework and $8,000 of recognized client credit-loss expense. These are modeled expenses, not an additional cash reserve or an assumption that every late invoice becomes a loss.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.detail: Treat this bar as the closing total. Non-direct operating expenses equal $224,000 annually, or approximately $18,666.67 monthly, inside the stated $5,000–$25,000 monthly operating range; direct contract delivery remains separately identified.

diagrams.title: Five Service Niches, One Recognized-Revenue Basis
diagrams.subtitle: Annual service fees per client; four clients in each niche.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Bar lengths show illustrative annual operator service fees per client in USD, not observed market prices, contract award values, or profit margins. Each client belongs to one primary service package; no client is counted in two bars.
diagrams.caption: Four clients per package yield $160,000 + $120,000 + $112,000 + $96,000 + $72,000 = $560,000. Package pricing must support documented work rather than payments for influence.

stages.label: Federal technical-services capture
stages.detail: Four clients contribute $160,000 through capability mapping, solicitation analysis, and recurring capture coordination. Invoice contracted monthly services; keep the client's technical solution and bid pricing under client ownership.

stages.label: Municipal facilities bid operations
stages.detail: Four clients contribute $120,000 through local portal monitoring, site-visit scheduling, document assembly, and amendment control. Maintain separate jurisdiction rules instead of applying federal clauses indiscriminately.

stages.label: Prime/sub teaming administration
stages.detail: Four clients contribute $112,000 through capability verification, workshare documentation, and teaming records. Charge for actual support work; review FAR 9.6, applicable pass-through clauses, and set-aside performance limits.

stages.label: Public-supply solicitation desk
stages.detail: Four clients contribute $96,000 through specification crosswalks, supplier confirmations, lead-time tracking, and bid assembly. Identify applicable domestic-source and nonmanufacturer requirements before pursuing supply awards.

stages.label: Post-submission administration
stages.detail: Four clients contribute $72,000 through status tracking, client-directed clarification coordination, document retention, and service reporting. Keep authorized government communications distinct from unsolicited access selling.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Accepting the Engagement
diagrams.subtitle: Each branch either proceeds with evidence or stops for redesign.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The numeric values indicate check sequence, not risk scores. Apply federal statutes and clauses according to their scope and the solicitation. For municipal work, identify local ethics and purchasing rules separately; federal funding can add requirements.
diagrams.caption: Run all four checks before promising services. A favorable result on fee structure does not resolve procurement integrity, kickbacks, or unlawful performance arrangements.

stages.label: Contingent-fee structure
stages.detail: Does compensation depend on securing a government contract? If yes, stop for analysis under 41 U.S.C. 3901, FAR Subpart 3.4, and applicable FAR 52.203-5 terms, including the narrowly defined bona fide employee or agency exception. If no, document service deliverables and continue.

stages.label: Procurement integrity
stages.detail: Does the work involve protected bid, proposal, or source selection information, or restricted employment contacts? If yes, stop the affected activity and obtain a documented resolution under 41 U.S.C. 2102–2104 and FAR 3.104. Otherwise record information provenance and continue.

stages.label: Kickbacks and influence
stages.value: Reject improper payments or preferential treatment
stages.detail: Is anything of value being offered for improper favorable treatment in a prime contract or related subcontract? If yes, reject the arrangement and address applicable reporting duties. Apply 41 U.S.C. 8702 and FAR Subpart 3.5; separately assess public-official bribery under 18 U.S.C. 201 where applicable.

stages.label: Performance and eligibility
stages.value: Proceed only with executable lawful workshare
stages.detail: Can the eligible contractor perform the required workshare and substantiate intermediary value? If no, redesign or decline. Evaluate 13 CFR 125.6, applicable FAR 52.219-14 and 52.215-23 terms, and ostensible-subcontractor exposure under 13 CFR 121.103(h). If yes, retain the calculation and responsibility matrix.

diagrams.title: Five Core Seats; Two Seats Added at Scale
diagrams.subtitle: Conservative and Base: 2 FT + 3 C. Scaled: 3 FT + 4 C.
diagrams.assumptions_note: FT means full-time employee; C means contractor seat with variable engagement hours. Each stage represents one seat, not one full-time equivalent. Seats six and seven exist only in the Scaled Small-Team scenario; headcount alone does not establish capacity.
diagrams.caption: Canonical annual outcomes: Conservative $120,000 revenue at 15% equals $18,000 owner net; Base $560,000 at 22.5% equals $126,000; Scaled $1,000,000 at 30% equals $300,000. Recognized service fees remain the revenue basis in every scenario.

stages.label: Managing operator
stages.value: Core seat one: full-time accountable lead
stages.detail: Own client selection, service pricing, conflict review, cash forecasting, and engagement scope. Approve pursuit capacity using actual hours and receivables rather than the nominal value of prospective client awards.

stages.label: Bid operations manager
stages.value: Core seat two: full-time workflow owner
stages.detail: Maintain solicitation alerts, bid calendars, version control, amendment tracking, and submission receipts. Escalate missed client inputs early enough to withdraw or revise a pursuit without a defective submission.

stages.label: Capture analyst
stages.value: Core seat three: contracted research specialist
stages.detail: Screen SAM.gov notices and municipal opportunities, map requirements to supplier capabilities, and maintain pursuit evidence. Distinguish public opportunity intelligence from protected procurement information.

stages.label: Proposal specialist
stages.value: Core seat four: contracted production specialist
stages.detail: Assemble response matrices, edit client-provided technical content, and check required attachments. Record unresolved claims for client correction instead of inventing past performance or unsupported qualifications.

stages.label: Supplier performance verifier
stages.value: Core seat five: contracted delivery specialist
stages.detail: Validate supplier commitments, lead times, workshare evidence, and delivery dependencies. Escalate supplier failure and substitution risk before the client commits to an unsupported performance schedule.

stages.label: Client delivery lead
stages.value: Scaled seat six: additional full-time employee
stages.detail: Add in the Scaled scenario to manage service acceptance, renewals, and cross-client workload. The resulting employee count is three; preserve separation between client award administration and operator service billing.

stages.label: Surge proposal specialist
stages.value: Scaled seat seven: additional contracted specialist
stages.detail: Add in the Scaled scenario for concurrent submission peaks and independent package checks. The resulting contractor count is four; schedule actual availability rather than assuming every contractor works full time.

diagrams.title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Pursuit Volume
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets across $25,000, $100,000, and $150,000 funding plans.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric bar values represent the selected $100,000 startup plan in USD. Each stage also specifies its $25,000 lean-plan and $150,000 upper-plan allocation. These are funding alternatives, not the Conservative, Base, or Scaled annual earnings scenarios.
diagrams.caption: Lean: $10,000 + $5,000 + $6,000 + $4,000 = $25,000. Selected: $40,000 + $20,000 + $25,000 + $15,000 = $100,000. Upper: $60,000 + $30,000 + $38,000 + $22,000 = $150,000.

stages.label: Working-capital runway
stages.detail: Hold cash for staged operating commitments and collection timing. At $5,000 monthly operating expense, these allocations cover two, eight, and twelve months before receipts; at $25,000 they cover 0.4, 1.6, and 2.4 months. Direct delivery costs can require additional cash.

stages.label: Contracting and risk setup
stages.detail: Fund scoped agreement review, insurance placement, entity administration, and jurisdiction-specific operating procedures. SAM.gov registration itself is free; any paid assistance must be separately described rather than represented as a government registration charge.

stages.label: Bid-desk systems and launch delivery
stages.detail: Fund secure document storage, access controls, CRM setup, calendar automation, and limited launch contractor work. Use SAM.gov alerts, Microsoft 365, and documented checklists before purchasing overlapping research subscriptions.

stages.label: Pipeline development
stages.detail: Fund targeted supplier outreach, capability interviews, industry meetings, and scoped proposal development. Model the stated 6–18 months to first deal; startup cash alone does not support every combination of that delay and the $5,000–$25,000 monthly operating range.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to an Evidence-Ready Bid Desk
diagrams.subtitle: Build operating readiness without assuming an award in the first month.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values identify milestone end days. The sprint establishes service scope, systems, and pursuit discipline; the canonical time to first deal remains 6–18 months. Client awards, signed engagements, recognized fees, and collected cash are separate events.
diagrams.caption: Advance on completed evidence: a service charter, an opportunity matrix, a tested submission workflow, and a dated pursuit plan.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Define one service niche and fee structure
stages.detail: Select one supplier segment and initial jurisdiction. Draft deliverables, exclusions, pricing, and client responsibilities; complete the four statutory checks. Produce a service charter, conflict register, and startup cash plan with explicit spending limits.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Build alerts, calendars, and opportunity evidence
stages.detail: Configure SAM.gov saved searches and relevant municipal portal monitoring. Review ten actual notices, record mandatory requirements and amendments, and assign calendar owners. Produce a dated opportunity matrix with documented reasons for pursuing or rejecting each notice.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Test supplier qualification and submission controls
stages.detail: Conduct five capability interviews and document delivery constraints. Run a mock submission using a public notice, without transmitting a bid. Test attachment naming, deadline time zones, client signoff, access recovery, and receipt retention.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Launch measured outreach and cash review
stages.detail: Issue service proposals only to qualified prospects with reviewed structures. Publish a ninety-day pursuit calendar and weekly receivables review. Record observed cohort conversion separately from the illustrative funnel; do not count outreach, bids, or client awards as earned fees.
